This strongly implies Tenerife is a significant island within the Canary Islands. I should try searching for "Tenerife" to get general information and hopefully confirm its population status within the Canary Islands.
Action 4: Search[Tenerife]
Observation 4: Tenerife (/ˌtɛnəˈriːf(eɪ)/ TEN-ə-REEF-(ay); Spanish: [teneˈɾife] ⓘ; formerly spelled Teneriffe) is the largest and most-populous island of the Canary Islands, an autonomous community of Spain.[5] With a land area of 2,034.38 km2 (785.48 mi2) and a population of 972,018 inhabitants as of January 2026[update],[6] it is the most-populous island in Spain[5] and the entire Macaronesia region. Tenerife is also home to 42.7% of the total population of the archipelago.[7]. More than seven million tourists (7,384,707 in 2024) visit Tenerife each year, making it by far the most visited island in the archipelago.[8] It is one of the most important tourist destinations in Spain[9] and the world,[10] hosting one of the world's largest carnivals, the Carnival of Santa Cruz de Tenerife.. The capital of the island, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, is also the seat of the island council (cabildo insular). The city and Las Palmas de Gran Canaria are the co-capitals of the autonomous community of the Canary Islands.
